claims.claim: Variants with nearly identical aromatic surface topologies, such as ScFlo11A and ScΣFlo11A, can clearly discriminate between each other when a further surface feature is added.
claims.source: Moreover, even variants with nearly identical aromatic surface topologies, such as ScFlo11A and ScΣFlo11A, can clearly discriminate between each other, given that a further surface feature is added, as exemplified by the Σ-specific insert.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the SCFS data showing discrimination between ScFlo11A and ScΣFlo11A.

claims.claim: In mammalian tissues and organs, teneurins, cadherins and nectins are well-studied adhesion molecules that confer homophilic and heterophilic cell-cell interactions by cis-clustering and trans-interactions.
claims.source: In mammalian tissues and organs, teneurins, cadherins and nectins are well-studied adhesion molecules that confer homophilic and heterophilic cell-cell interactions by cis-clustering and trans-interactions (Rikitake et al., 2012; Beckmann et al., 2013; Gul et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research on mammalian adhesion molecules.

claims.claim: Protocadherins confer neuronal self-recognition involving separate domains for cis- and trans-interactions.
claims.source: For protocadherins, a specialized family of cadherins, structural and functional as well as biophysical investigations have recently shown that these multi-domain cell-surface proteins confer neuronal self-recognition involving separate domains for cis- and trans-interactions (Rubinstein et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research on protocadherins.

claims.claim: Flo11-mediated cell-cell adhesion involves trans-interactions of collectives of Flo11 molecules formed by cis-clustering.
claims.source: However, previous data suggests that Flo11-mediated cell-cell adhesion involves trans-interactions of collectives of Flo11 molecules formed by cis-clustering, rather than multiple bimolecular trans-interactions of Flo11 adhesins that do not interact in cis (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: This claim is speculated based on previous ultrastructural data and the current mutational analysis.

claims.claim: Ultrastructural analysis of Flo11-Flo11 contact sites supports the view that Flo11 proteins form co-aligned fibers at the cell surface by clustering of Flo11 molecules in cis.
claims.source: Here, our previous ultrastructural analysis of Flo11-Flo11 contact sites support the view that Flo11 proteins form co-aligned fibers at the cell surface by clustering of Flo11 molecules in cis (Kraushaar et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previously published ultrastructural data.

claims.claim: The formation of Flo11 clusters could be mediated by cis-interaction of Flo11B domains via beta-aggregation-prone amyloid-forming sequences.
claims.source: Moreover, the formation of such clusters could be mediated by cis-interaction of Flo11B domains via beta-aggregation-prone amyloid-forming sequences (Ramsook et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is speculated based on published data about Flo11B domains.

claims.claim: Flo11 variants that carry mutations in either aromatic band I or band II are only partially abrogated for single cell-cell adhesion in homotypic configurations.
claims.source: Here, we found that Flo11 variants that carry mutations in either aromatic band I (I) or band II (II) are only partially abrogated for single cell-cell adhesion in homotypic configurations, whereas a complete loss of adhesion is observed in heterotypic measurements.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SCFS data presented in the study.

claims.claim: A complete loss of adhesion is observed in heterotypic measurements when Flo11 variants carry mutations in either aromatic band I or band II.
claims.source: Here, we found that Flo11 variants that carry mutations in either aromatic band I (I) or band II (II) are only partially abrogated for single cell-cell adhesion in homotypic configurations, whereas a complete loss of adhesion is observed in heterotypic measurements.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SCFS data presented in the study.

claims.claim: Productive adhesive forces can be achieved by either I-I or II-II trans-interactions, but not by I-II interactions.
claims.source: This finding supports a model, in which productive adhesive forces can be achieved by either I-I or II-II trans-interactions, but they do not support the occurrence of I-II interactions.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the mutational analysis data.

claims.claim: Flo11 molecules must be tethered in cis before either I-I or II-II trans-interactions take place.
claims.source: This further implies that Flo11 molecules must be tethered in cis before either I-I or II-II trans-interactions take place, given that a free choice between I-I or II-II would be assumed in the case of only bimolecular trans-interactions, which is not in agreement with the complete loss of adhesive forces observed in the heterotypic situation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the mutational analysis data and the model of Flo11 interactions.

claims.claim: The efficiency of biofilm formation as measured by the total size does not necessarily correlate with cell-cell adhesion forces.
claims.source: Our analysis of biofilm development indicates that in contrast to the formation of multicellular aggregates, the efficiency of biofilm formation as measured by the total size does not necessarily correlate with cell-cell adhesion forces.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of SCFS and biofilm size data.

claims.claim: ScFlo11A confers roughly 1.4-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces than ClFlo11A.
claims.source: This is exemplified by comparing the properties of ScFlo11 and ClFlo11 adhesion domains in non-competitive situations. Here, ScFlo11A confers roughly 1.4-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces, but on average leads to 1.8-fold lower biofilm sizes, when compared to ClFlo11A.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SCFS data presented in the study.

claims.claim: ScFlo11A leads to 1.8-fold lower biofilm sizes on average when compared to ClFlo11A.
claims.source: This is exemplified by comparing the properties of ScFlo11 and ClFlo11 adhesion domains in non-competitive situations. Here, ScFlo11A confers roughly 1.4-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces, but on average leads to 1.8-fold lower biofilm sizes, when compared to ClFlo11A.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by biofilm size data presented in the study.

claims.claim: ClFlo11A might be able to interact with the substrate much more efficiently than ScFlo11A.
claims.source: This apparent discrepancy could be explained by postulating significant differences in cell-substrate adhesion conferred by these Flo11A variants. In other words, ClFlo11A might be able to interact with the substrate much more efficiently than ScFlo11A and thereby confer a significantly better spreading of the growing biofilm.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculated to explain the discrepancy between cell-cell adhesion forces and biofilm sizes.

claims.claim: Strong adhesion can correlate with dominance against less adhesive cells in competitive biofilms.
claims.source: Our study also reveals that strong adhesion can correlate with dominance against less adhesive cells. This is exemplified by the ScΣFlo11A variant, which in competitive assays dominates against all other Flo11 variants tested and confers roughly 2-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces in comparison to its competitors.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by competitive biofilm assay and SCFS data.

claims.claim: ScΣFlo11A confers roughly 2-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces in comparison to its competitors.
claims.source: This is exemplified by the ScΣFlo11A variant, which in competitive assays dominates against all other Flo11 variants tested and confers roughly 2-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces in comparison to its competitors.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SCFS data presented in the study.

claims.claim: KpFlo11A shows clear dominance over ScFlo11A in competitive biofilms, although ScFlo11A confers roughly 1.5-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces.
claims.source: When comparing ScFlo11A with KpFlo11A, however, our study reveals a clear dominance of KpFlo11A, although ScFlo11A confers roughly 1.5-fold higher cell-cell adhesion forces.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by competitive biofilm assay and SCFS data.

claims.claim: ScFlo11A and KpFlo11A produce biofilms of comparable sizes indicating that cell-substrate adhesion forces are comparable.
claims.source: Moreover, both variants produce biofilms of comparable sizes indicating that cell-substrate adhesion forces are comparable.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from biofilm size data.

claims.claim: The function of Flo11-type proteins in conferring kin-directed cell-cell aggregation and discrimination can be observed in several families of Saccharomycetales.
claims.source: Finally, our study has revealed that the function of Flo11-type proteins in conferring kin-directed cell-cell aggregation and discrimination can be observed in several families of Saccharomycetales.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the functional data from multiple Flo11A variants from different yeast families.

claims.claim: The importance of Flo11-type adhesins for building multicellular consortia for kin-directed protection or other types of cooperative interaction appears to be conserved.
claims.source: Thus, the importance of these adhesins for building multicellular consortia for kin-directed protection or other types of cooperative interaction appears to be conserved.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the conservation of Flo11A function across different yeast species.

claims.claim: Flo11-directed kin discrimination could be accomplished at sub-species level by a single genetic event, as exemplified by the Σ-insert.
claims.source: Moreover, our study suggests that Flo11-directed kin discrimination could be accomplished at sub-species level by a single genetic event, as exemplified by the Σ-insert.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the functional data showing that the Σ-insert is sufficient to transfer allele-specific discrimination.

claims.claim: Variants carrying the Σ-insert are present only in the 'Sake' lineage of non-mosaic S. cerevisiae strains.
claims.source: Our finding that variants carrying this insert are present only in the 'Sake' lineage of non-mosaic S. cerevisiae strains, further opens the possibility that Σ-like sub-domains originate from the domestication of sake yeast strains.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis data.

claims.claim: Σ-like sub-domains might originate from the domestication of sake yeast strains.
claims.source: Our finding that variants carrying this insert are present only in the 'Sake' lineage of non-mosaic S. cerevisiae strains, further opens the possibility that Σ-like sub-domains originate from the domestication of sake yeast strains.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculated based on the phylogenetic distribution of the Σ-insert.

results.result: Flo11A domains from diverse yeast species display high sequence variability, with S. cerevisiae Flo11A alleles well separated from other Saccharomycetales except S. paradoxus. A unique 15-amino acid insert is found exclusively in 19 of 52 S. cerevisiae Flo11A alleles from the 'Sake' lineage.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C38 are supported by phylogenetic analysis and sequence alignment data shown in figures. The sequence variability, phylogenetic separation, and lineage-specific insert are documented with appropriate data visualization. The identification of S. paradoxus as the closest relative is supported by citations to established phylogenetic studies.

results.result: All tested Flo11A domains from diverse yeast species confer adhesive growth despite sequence identities as low as 18% to ScFlo11A, indicating that the capacity for cellular adhesion is highly conserved in Saccharomycetales.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C40 are supported by adhesive growth assay data shown in supplementary figures. The functional conservation despite low sequence identity is a reasonable inference from the experimental data. However, the claim of conservation across all Saccharomycetales is extrapolated from a limited sample of 8 tested variants.

results.result: ScFlo11A mediates strong homotypic cell-cell adhesion with average maximum forces of 13.4 nN after 20s contact, nearly an order of magnitude higher than heterotypic interactions. Adhesion forces establish within the first second and increase steadily up to 20s, with actual forces likely exceeding 13.4 nN.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C46 are well-supported by SCFS measurements shown in Figure 2D and supplementary data. The kinetic measurements provide temporal resolution, and the inference that forces exceed 13.4 nN is reasonable given that probe cells were torn from cantilevers at longer contact times. Statistical significance is demonstrated.

results.result: ScFlo11A-presenting cells form large aggregates covering up to 1 mm², over 1000-fold larger than cells lacking ScFlo11A. There is a clear correlation between single-cell adhesion forces and population-level cell aggregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C49 are supported by QCAM data in Figure 2E. The correlation between single-cell forces and population aggregation (C49) is demonstrated by Figure 7 showing Spearman correlation. The quantitative measurements and statistical analysis support these conclusions.

results.result: ScFlo11A contains sixteen conserved aromatic residues arranged in two surface bands (I and II). Systematic mutagenesis identified twelve residues involved in adhesive growth. Mutations in either band alone reduce adhesion, while combined mutations in both bands abrogate adhesion, suggesting the bands directly interact.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C63 are supported by structural data (Figure 3A), systematic mutagenesis (Figure 3, supplementary figures), SCFS measurements, and QCAM analysis. The inference that bands directly interact (C63) is reasonable but speculative, based on the pattern of mutational effects. The experimental design is rigorous with appropriate controls.

results.result: The crystal structure of KpFlo11A (1.40 Å resolution) shows high structural similarity to ScFlo11A (r.m.s.d. 1.01 Å) despite only 32% sequence identity. The FNIII core domain is highly conserved, while apical regions are more variable. Both structures display similar but not identical aromatic band arrangements with rigid surfaces.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C73 are supported by crystallographic data (Supplementary files 4-5), structural comparisons (Figure 4), and ConSurf analysis. The structural similarity despite low sequence identity is well-documented. B-factor analysis supports surface rigidity claims. The inference of functional conservation from structural conservation is reasonable.

results.result: ScFlo11A and KpFlo11A both undergo efficient homophilic interactions in vitro (KD 19.5 µM and 31.8 µM respectively), but show weaker heterophilic binding (KD 121.1 µM). Kinetic analysis reveals comparable dissociation rates but significantly lower association rates for heterophilic interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C80 are supported by SPR data shown in Figure 4B and supplementary figures. The measurements are performed in at least duplicate with appropriate controls. The kinetic analysis distinguishes between association and dissociation contributions to binding affinity. The inference of discrimination capability is well-supported by the quantitative differences.

results.result: KpFlo11A and ClFlo11A confer efficient homotypic cell-cell adhesion and aggregation comparable to ScFlo11A. However, heterotypic interactions between different Flo11A variants show clearly reduced adhesion forces, demonstrating discrimination capability.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C85 are supported by SCFS data (Figure 4C) and QCAM analysis (Figure 4D). Multiple Flo11A variants are tested in both homotypic and heterotypic configurations with appropriate statistical analysis. The discrimination capability is consistently demonstrated across variant pairs.

results.result: In competitive biofilm assays, homotypic biofilms show low strain ratios at the outer edge with sectoring indicating genetic drift. Heterotypic biofilms show significantly higher ratios with one allele monopolizing the biofilm edge, demonstrating kin discrimination in heterogeneous populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C94 are supported by competitive biofilm data (Figure 5, supplementary figures). The distinction between homotypic and heterotypic biofilms is clear and statistically significant. The inference of genetic drift in homotypic biofilms is supported by citation. Spatial analysis confirms allele dominance patterns. At least two biological replicates were tested.

results.result: ScΣFlo11A contains a 15-amino acid Σ-insert near aromatic band I. This variant shows enhanced adhesive growth, significantly higher homotypic adhesion forces (~2-fold), and stronger aggregation compared to ScFlo11A, but cannot interact with ScFlo11A or other species variants in heterotypic configurations.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C102 are supported by molecular modeling (Figure 6A), adhesive growth assays, SCFS measurements (Figure 6B), and QCAM analysis (Figure 6C). The structural location of the insert is based on modeling, which is less definitive than crystal structure but reasonable. Functional differences are well-documented with statistical significance.

results.result: The synthetic variant ScFlo11AΣins, created by inserting the Σ-insert into ScFlo11A, is fully functional for adhesive growth, homotypic interaction, and aggregation. Critically, it interacts with ScΣFlo11A but not ScFlo11A, demonstrating that the Σ-insert alone is sufficient to transfer allele-specific discrimination.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C108 are supported by functional assays (Figure 6B-C, supplementary figures). The synthetic variant experiment is a strong test of sufficiency. The claim that the insert is sufficient (C108) is well-supported, though the variant still differs by 11 amino acids from native ScΣFlo11A, which is appropriately noted.

results.result: ScΣFlo11A outcompetes all other tested Flo11A variants in competitive biofilms, dominating both the outer edge and the whole biofilm area. This demonstrates that Flo11A can confer allele-specific discrimination at the sub-species level.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C111 are supported by competitive biofilm data (Figure 5, supplementary figures). The dominance of ScΣFlo11A is consistently observed across multiple comparisons. The inference of sub-species discrimination (C111) is well-supported by the combined evidence from SCFS, QCAM, and competitive biofilm assays.

results.result: Flo11-type adhesins from diverse yeasts confer kin discrimination at both species and sub-species levels through efficient homotypic cell-cell adhesion and discrimination against non-kin variants in heterotypic situations in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C116 represent the main conclusions of the study, supported by the combined evidence from SCFS, QCAM, and competitive biofilm assays across multiple Flo11A variants. The multi-scale approach (single cell to population to biofilm) provides strong converging evidence. Statistical significance is demonstrated throughout.

results.result: High-resolution structural analysis shows that highly divergent Flo11A domains have similar core and aromatic surface patterns. In vitro functional analysis demonstrates that different Flo11A variants discriminate between homophilic and heterophilic interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C118 are supported by crystallographic data comparing ScFlo11A and KpFlo11A structures and SPR measurements showing differential binding affinities. The structural similarity despite sequence divergence is well-documented, and the discrimination in vitro is quantitatively demonstrated.

results.result: FLO11-type domains fulfill important criteria for single greenbeard genes, which confer benefits by homophilic interactions to cells carrying the allele.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C120 are supported by the functional data showing homophilic interaction-dependent benefits and appropriate citations to the greenbeard gene concept. The inference is reasonable given the demonstrated properties of Flo11A domains, though the full evolutionary implications would require additional population-level studies.

results.result: Flo11A domains in certain yeast species confer adhesion forces >25 nN after 20s contact time, considerably higher than adhesion forces measured between mammalian cells at similar contact times.
results.evaluation: Claims C132-C133 are supported by SCFS data and comparison with cited mammalian cell adhesion studies. The comparison is appropriate given similar experimental conditions (contact time). The claim is conservative given that measurements were limited by technical constraints (cells torn from cantilever).

results.result: Quantitative SCFS data correlates with phenotypes in homogeneous populations analyzed by QCAM, demonstrating that adhesion forces between cells determine macroscopic aggregate sizes.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-C135 are supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7 (Spearman's rho = 0.85, p < 0.001). The correlation is strong and statistically significant. The causal inference (C135) is reasonable but should be interpreted carefully as correlation does not prove causation, though the mechanistic link is plausible.

results.result: Flo11A domains confer cell-cell adhesion through aromatic surface residues in a more specific manner than unspecific hydrophobins. The precise topology of aromatic residues is important for molecular discrimination, as variants with similar topologies can discriminate when additional surface features are added.
results.evaluation: Claims C136-C142 are supported by mutational analysis, structural comparisons, and functional data. The model of hydrophobin-like interactions is based on previous work (C136). The specificity beyond simple hydrophobic interactions is demonstrated by differential homo- vs. heterotypic binding. Some claims (C138, C140) are appropriately speculative.

results.result: Flo11-mediated cell-cell adhesion likely involves trans-interactions of Flo11 molecule collectives formed by cis-clustering, rather than multiple bimolecular trans-interactions. Mutational analysis suggests Flo11 molecules must be tethered in cis before trans-interactions occur, with productive forces achieved by either I-I or II-II interactions but not I-II.
results.evaluation: Claims C145-C151 present a mechanistic model based on previous ultrastructural data (C146), published speculation about Flo11B domains (C147), and current mutational analysis (C148-C151). While the mutational data support the model, direct evidence for cis-clustering and the proposed interaction mechanism is limited. The model is plausible but requires additional experimental validation such as cross-linking studies or higher-resolution structural analysis of Flo11 assemblies.

results.result: Biofilm formation efficiency (total size) does not necessarily correlate with cell-cell adhesion forces. ScFlo11A confers 1.4-fold higher adhesion forces but 1.8-fold lower biofilm sizes compared to ClFlo11A, possibly due to differences in cell-substrate adhesion.
results.evaluation: Claims C152-C154 are supported by comparison of SCFS and biofilm size data. The lack of correlation is clearly demonstrated. The speculation about cell-substrate adhesion differences (C155) is reasonable but untested. This highlights the complexity of biofilm formation beyond cell-cell adhesion alone.

results.result: Strong adhesion can correlate with dominance in competitive biofilms, as ScΣFlo11A dominates with ~2-fold higher adhesion forces. However, KpFlo11A dominates over ScFlo11A despite ScFlo11A having 1.5-fold higher adhesion forces, suggesting other factors contribute to competitive success.
results.evaluation: Claims C156-C159 are supported by competitive biofilm and SCFS data. The complexity of competitive outcomes is appropriately acknowledged. The observation that adhesion force alone does not predict competitive success (C158-C159) is important and suggests additional factors like cell-substrate adhesion or growth rates may be involved.

results.result: The function of Flo11-type proteins in conferring kin-directed cell-cell aggregation and discrimination is conserved across several Saccharomycetales families. Sub-species discrimination can be accomplished by single genetic events like the Σ-insert, which is found only in the 'Sake' lineage and may originate from domestication.
results.evaluation: Claims C160-C163 are supported by functional data from multiple yeast families and phylogenetic analysis. The conservation of function is well-demonstrated. The speculation about domestication origins (C164) is appropriately tentative and based on the phylogenetic distribution. Further evolutionary analysis would strengthen this claim.

results.result: Background on kin discrimination: The ability to discriminate kin from non-kin is fundamental for social organisms and has evolved across diverse taxa. Cell surface adhesins have been suggested to mediate kin discrimination in microorganisms, but the molecular and structural basis is largely unexplored. Yeasts are ideal models with Flo11 as a candidate adhesin.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C35 provide background context supported by appropriate citations to established literature. These claims set up the rationale for the study and are well-supported by prior work. The assessment of gaps in knowledge (C15, C21) appropriately motivates the current research.

results.result: Comparison with other kin discrimination systems: Flo11A represents the first fungal adhesin mediating kin discrimination by homophilic interaction at both species and sub-species levels. Other systems (PA14/Flo5, csaA, TgrB1/TgrC1, TraA) use different mechanisms and lack the biophysical and structural characterization provided here.
results.evaluation: Claims C121-C131 appropriately contextualize the novelty of the findings through comparison with other systems. The citations support the descriptions of other kin discrimination mechanisms. The claim of being the first fungal example with this level of characterization (C121, C131) appears justified based on the cited literature.

results.result: Comparison with mammalian adhesion molecules: In mammalian systems, teneurins, cadherins, nectins, and protocadherins mediate cell-cell interactions through cis-clustering and trans-interactions, with protocadherins using separate domains for each type of interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C143-C144 provide comparative context from mammalian systems, supported by appropriate citations. This comparison helps frame the potential mechanisms for Flo11A function, though the authors appropriately note that direct evidence for similar mechanisms in Flo11 is limited.
